text:
Ever wondered how your database finds one row among ten million so fast? It uses an index, which works like the index at the back of a textbook. Instead of flipping through every page to find a topic, you jump straight to the right spot.

Most indexes are built on a B-tree, which makes lookups O(log n). Doubling your data adds only one more step to the search, not twice as many. In one real-world case, a query on a 10M-row table dropped from 2.1 seconds to 4 milliseconds.

Indexes do have a cost. They can slow down writes by about 15%, because the database has to update them on every insert and update. The rest of this piece covers how indexes work, when they help, and how to use them without paying more than you need to.
